name: Parallels
summary: Parallels Desktop runs Windows, Linux and macOS in a virtual machine on a Mac, with Standard, Pro and Business editions for home users, developers and teams.
best_for: Mac users who need to run Windows apps next to macOS apps, from home users on Standard to developers on Pro and small teams on Business
skip_if: you need a free tool (VirtualBox-type options exist), run an Intel Mac that the latest version does not support, or only need a few web-based Windows apps
honest_knock: Your Windows licence is a separate cost and is not included in any edition. The headline prices change with promotions: on the day we read the page Standard was €49.99 against a €99.99 list price, and the renewal price is the thing to check. Each licence covers one Mac, renewal payments are not returnable, and the latest major version does not come free with a one-time licence.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Standard · Standard subscription list price per year for one Mac, 8 GB vRAM and 4 vCPUs per virtual machine
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-08 in a live browser on parallels.com/products/desktop/buy, euros from a Netherlands connection) Parallels Desktop runs Windows, Linux or macOS in a virtual machine on a Mac. Three editions are sold as yearly subscriptions. Standard is €99.99 a year (8 GB virtual RAM and 4 virtual CPUs per machine), Pro is €119.99 a year (128 GB and 32 CPUs, command line tools and developer features) and Business is €149.99 a year (Pro plus central administration, volume licensing and deployment through Mac management tools). On the day we read the page a Black Friday offer cut these to €49.99, €59.99 and €97.49 a year; it is a promotion, so check the number at checkout. Pro and Business can also be bought as a 2-year subscription. The page lists a one-time purchase option for Standard, and the Standard card says subscription only for the latest version features. Each licence covers one Mac, and a Windows licence is not included. All purchases carry a 30-day money-back guarantee; the vendor's help centre says renewal payments are not returnable. Enterprise pricing is by contact.
